name: Philtrum filler / shortening

card.summary: Reshaping the philtrum and cupid's bow with filler or a lip lift to look shorter and more defined; plenty of cosmetic practice, little formal evidence.
card.aka: Philtrum lift; lip lift; cupid's bow filler
card.note: Surgical versions leave scars; filler carries standard filler risks.

quick.overview:
The philtrum is the groove between the nose and upper lip. Some people seek a shorter philtrum or a sharper cupid's bow, using filler along the lip border or a surgical lip lift.

Surgeons report high satisfaction with lip lifts, but no single technique is standard.[3]
quick.mechanism: Filler adds volume at the lip border and philtral columns. A lip lift removes skin below the nose or along the lip border to expose more of the upper lip; a 2014 review found philtrum length decreased with indirect techniques.[3]
quick.risks: Lip lift risks include visible scarring, numbness, asymmetry, lip distortion and speech or smile changes.[3] Filler carries bruising, lumps, allergic reactions and, rarely, vascular complications.[2]

lead: The philtrum is the vertical groove in the middle of the upper lip, running from the base of the nose to the lip's upper edge.[1] The cupid's bow is the double curve of the upper lip's border, with peaks lining up with the philtral columns.[5]

Philtrum filler and shortening refer to cosmetic efforts to make this area look shorter, more defined or more lifted, either by injecting filler or by surgical lip lift. Wikipedia's lip lift article describes surgery that makes the vermilion border more prominent and changes the area above the lip.[3]
Published information located for this article is descriptive and surgical; no trial specific to filler shortening of the philtrum was identified.
infobox: Filler; direct or subnasal lip lift

paras: The philtrum forms where embryonic processes meet; incomplete fusion can cause cleft lip.[1] A flattened or smooth philtrum can accompany certain conditions such as fetal alcohol syndrome.[1] The upper-lip vermilion border forms the cupid's bow.[4][5]
Fillers, commonly hyaluronic acid, are used in the lips to add volume and definition; overfilling can give an exaggerated appearance and under-injection can leave ridges.[2][6]

Surgical lip lifts include the direct lift, which removes skin at the white roll, and the subnasal bullhorn lift, which removes tissue under the nose. Corner lifts and V-Y augmentation are other variants.[3] A 2014 review found philtrum length decreased with indirect techniques but not with V-Y augmentation.[3]

Lip lift complications listed include numbness, stiffness, lip distortion, smile deformation, speech changes and visible or hypertrophic scarring, especially at the white roll. Swelling usually settles in one to two weeks and tightness can last two to four months.[3]
Filler complications include bruising, swelling, lumps, infection and rare vascular events.[2]

A short philtrum is discussed by some appearance communities as a youthful or attractive feature. Because published community discussion is limited, this article does not document specific forum claims.
No studies found. Surgical case series and reviews of lip lift techniques exist, summarized only secondarily here.[3]
